name: AI Deep Dive — QBTS — 2026-05-04
rationale: D-Wave Quantum (QBTS) at $21.60 trades at ~325x TTM revenue of $24.6M and $8.0B market cap. D-Wave is fundamentally different from IONQ and RGTI — it uses quantum annealing rather than gate-based quantum computing. This limits its addressable market to optimization problems (logistics, scheduling, molecular simulation) but enables real commercial applications today. The standout metric is an 82.6% gross margin — the highest in the sector — suggesting premium pricing power in its niche. However, revenue growth decelerated to 19% after flat years ($8.8M→$8.8M→$24.6M), and net losses of -$355M on $24.6M revenue reflect extreme R&D intensity. The DCF model (FV $0.90) yields -96% implied downside. The investment case is narrow: D-Wave must prove that quantum annealing is superior to classical ML for a broad enough optimization market to justify its $8B valuation.

bear.rationale: Bear: Classical ML and simulated annealing improvements close the gap on D-Wave's optimization advantage. Revenue growth stalls at 10% CAGR as enterprises opt for free/cheap classical alternatives. Net losses remain extreme (-40%) as R&D and hardware costs dwarf revenue. Heavy dilution required for survival. QM 0.75: quantum annealing is a limited niche — cannot address the full QC market, and classical alternatives are improving fast.

base.rationale: Base: D-Wave carves out a defensible optimization-as-a-service niche for logistics, scheduling, and molecular simulation. Revenue reaches ~$110M by year 5. Stellar gross margins (82.6% TTM) convert to operating profitability as opex scales sub-linearly. 8% net margin by year 5. exitPE 35x on a niche profitable platform. Customers include governments and large enterprises with complex scheduling problems.

bull.rationale: Bull: Quantum annealing proves decisive for a broad class of NP-hard optimization problems — pharma drug discovery, financial portfolio optimization, supply chain. D-Wave becomes the de facto optimization infrastructure for enterprises that cannot wait for gate-based QC. Revenue scales to ~$270M by year 5 with 18% net margin from SaaS-like delivery. QM 1.05: proprietary annealing architecture has no direct quantum-native competitor in its niche. Catalyst: Landmark pharma or logistics optimization proof-of-value with quantified ROI.

aiThesis.rationale: D-Wave (QBTS) at $21.60 vs DCF FV $0.90 implies -96% downside on a 5-year model. The standout positive is 82.6% gross margin — the best in sector — suggesting premium pricing in its optimization niche. But $24.6M revenue growing 19% cannot justify $8B market cap. The technology risk is distinct: quantum annealing cannot solve all QC problems (gate-based is the general solution), and classical ML is improving fast on the same optimization problems D-Wave targets. Of the three quantum names (RGTI/IONQ/QBTS), QBTS has the worst revenue scale and most limited technology addressable market, partially offset by the strongest gross margin profile. The investment case requires the optimization-as-a-service market becoming large enough — and classical alternatives failing to compete — which is the lowest-probability bull case of the three.
